issues.description: Fast-path regex narrows the contract of the walker without documenting the precondition
issues.detail: The rule's implicit contract is: 'for each declaration whose value contains a time, validate it.' The new HAS_TIME guard correctly preserves that contract — every value rejected by /\dm?s/i provably cannot contain a CSS <time> token (which requires a digit followed by 's' or 'ms'). The substitution is sound, but the precondition is now load-bearing and undocumented; a one-line comment stating 'skip values that cannot contain a <time> token' would make the contract visible at the boundary so a future maintainer extending time syntax (e.g. unit-less zero handling, calc()) does not silently weaken the postcondition.

HAS_TIME asserts 'this value contains a time'; the regex actually asserts the weaker 'this value may contain a time token.' That is exactly the right strength for a cheap pre-filter, but the name promises more than it delivers. Renaming to MAY_CONTAIN_TIME or POSSIBLY_HAS_TIME would align the identifier with its actual postcondition and prevent a future caller from treating it as a definitive predicate.

review.summary: ADT-SOUND with minor SPEC-MISSING notes. The abstract data type here is the declaration walker, whose contract is 'flag time values below the minimum'; the patch adds a cheap pre-filter that provably cannot reject any value containing a CSS <time> token, so substitutability with the prior implementation holds and the postcondition is preserved. No LSP violation, no leaky abstraction, no boundary problem — the module boundary (rule function over PostCSS root) is unchanged and the filter lives correctly inside it. Two P2 notes only: the load-bearing precondition of the regex is undocumented, and its name (HAS_TIME) is slightly stronger than the predicate it actually computes. Safe to merge; the spec hygiene suggestions are for the long-lived-codebase discipline, not for correctness.
